summary: Implemented PF_HLINK in xs-rs: DIR entries and DATA file attributes now carry the C++ hdev/ino/nlink/ctime/ctime_ns fields, -H negotiates the feature, and the receiver groups source inodes, sends each group's data once, links aliases after transfer, and itemizes them exactly as the C++ xs does. Cross-direction C++/Rust push, pull and local copies preserve hard-link topology, including symlink and FIFO aliases.
diagnosis: Most of the work went into reading src/hardlink.cpp and remote.cpp and reproducing hardlink_finalize's anchor selection and output rows, not into transport changes. Measurements: the 5 new interop tests and 3 byte-pinned unit tests pass against the supplied C++ binary; manual -aH -i comparisons for C++ client push, C++ sender pull, Rust client push and local copy are identical to the C++ xs output; the C++ client reports one regular file transferred for four linked names and zero when a new name is added. All four required gate commands exited 0.
change: Added put_hlink/get_hlink, Attrs inode fields and HardlinkKey to rs/xs-rs/src/protocol.rs; populated them in scan.rs; added -H/--hard-links and HLINK negotiation in cli.rs/main.rs; added the receiver's hard-link registry, follower skipping, link publication and C++-matching finalizer in transfer.rs. Also changed ffi.rs's local_time buffer from [i8; 64] to [c_char; 64] so the required aarch64 check passes.
expected_effect: Hard-linked names now arrive as one inode in both directions and on local copies, with data sent once per group and itemization matching the C++ xs. Peers that do not negotiate PF_HLINK keep separate files, and a client asking for -H refuses a peer that cannot honor it before creating the destination.
risks: Hard-link behavior is covered for regular files, symlinks and FIFOs. Dry-run and --inplace remain pre-existing no-ops in xs-rs, so C++ hardlink_test cases that depend on those options may still differ. No performance benchmark was attempted for this protocol step.
tests: Added rs/xs-rs/tests/hardlink.rs with 5 tests (C++ push stats/topology/new name, Rust push, Rust pull, local copy, unnegotiated peer) and 3 protocol unit tests pinning HLINK field bytes and ordering. Ran XS_BIN=~/benchmarks/lab/engineer/XR10201808-hlink/parent/build/xs cargo test --manifest-path rs/Cargo.toml (all pass, including 5 hardlink tests), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; all four exited 0.
cpp_lesson: No C++ performance change follows from this step: hardlink_finalize's anchor and itemization rules were matched rather than replaced. The only portability correction was on the Rust side, using c_char rather than i8 for the strftime buffer.
commit_title: Port PF_HLINK hard-link preservation to xs-rs
commit_body: Port case XR10201808-hlink, step 7: PF_HLINK. Carry hdev, ino, nlink, ctime and ctime_ns in DIR entries and DATA file attributes with the C++ field order; negotiate PF_HLINK only with -H; group receiver members by source identity and publish hard links after data, following only new names and matching hardlink_finalize's anchor selection and itemized rows. Add byte-pinned unit tests and C++/Rust interop tests for push, pull, local copies and unnegotiated peers. Fix the aarch64 c_char buffer in local_time so the arm64 check passes.
